result.title: When Zero Is Competitive: A Descriptive Pilot of Transformer and Gate-Graph Surrogates on Random-Angle Quantum Circuits
result.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Descriptive pilot study. Exact experimental evidence archive currently private
result.summary: We examine supervised classical prediction of all one-qubit Z and two-qubit ZZ expectation values on noiseless, layered 4-10-qubit RX/RY/RZ-CNOT circuits. In a 63-cell stratified workload with disjoint circuit-template tests, we evaluate one transformer encoder and gate-dependency graph neural networks against literal-zero and training-derived constant predictors. On the Arm K training labels, 44.89% of scalar targets have absolute magnitude below 0.05. The held-out-template zero predictor has equal-instance mean absolute error 0.193399, and none of the evaluated transformer checkpoints or final graph-network endpoints achieves a lower score. A separate product-state positive control achieves MAE 0.007755 versus 0.514811 for zero, but does not explain the failure on the entangled workload. The difference between zero and a training-fitted mean constant under training MSE is only 0.14%, a descriptive point estimate without uncertainty analysis. The transformer's 815,233-parameter source identity is locally verified; detailed packed-input semantics have not been independently audited. These results constitute a descriptive pilot, not a causal explanation, formal equivalence test, or impossibility claim. Comparable circuits can be regenerated from the workload specification, but exact frozen datasets and model-run evidence remain private.

AI.brief_summary: 在无噪声的 4–10 比特分层量子电路上，用 transformer 编码器与门依赖图网络监督预测单比特 Z 与双比特 ZZ 期望值，并与恒零及训练拟合常数基线对比，发现所评估模型均未低于零预测器的误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 近半数目标幅值接近零、学习模型却不敌恒零基线，这一诊断思路可供核查 LVR 中「模型是否真正使用输入、是否退化为常数或先验」的基线与评估设计，但与视觉推理本体无直接关联，属较远线索。
